slides.text:
The `strings` package holds the everyday helpers for text: searching, splitting, trimming and replacing. Each one takes a string and returns a new value, because a Go string never changes.

In this module you will search, split and join, clean the edges and swap pieces. Building a long text piece by piece is `string-builder`.

Most functions take the text first and the piece to look for second. Some answer yes or no, others give a position.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
has = contains(text, piece)
      -> true or false
where = index(text, piece)
      -> position, or -1

slides.text: A position counts bytes, like `len` and slicing. A missing piece gives -1 and no error, so check it before you cut with it.

exercises.title: Search inside a string
exercises.guide: Test whether a string holds a piece, starts with it or ends with it.

chunks.guide: `Contains` answers true or false: is the piece anywhere in the string?

notes.text: The package name comes first, then the function.

chunks.guide: `ContainsAny` is true if any one of the characters appears. `ContainsRune` looks for a single rune.

notes.text: Each character of the second string is tried alone.
Takes one rune, not a string.

chunks.guide: `HasPrefix` and `HasSuffix` only look at the start and the end.

notes.text: True only if the string ends exactly with it.

exercises.title: Check a file name
exercises.guide: Check that the name starts with main, ends with .go and has _test somewhere in it.

exercises.title: Find the position
exercises.guide: Get the position of a piece, and use it to cut out part of the string.

chunks.guide: `Index` gives the byte where the first match starts.

notes.text: Position of the first match, counted in bytes.

chunks.guide: `LastIndex` starts the search from the end.
A piece that is not there gives -1, not an error.
Use the position of the last dot to cut out the extension.

exercises.title: Count and compare
exercises.guide: Count how often a piece appears, and compare ignoring upper and lower case.

chunks.guide: `Count` returns how many times the piece appears, without overlaps.

notes.text: Number of non-overlapping matches.

chunks.guide: An empty piece matches between every character: the character count plus one.
`==` is case sensitive. `EqualFold` ignores the case of letters.

notes.text: Compares letters as if both were the same case.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the output.
exercises.explanation: `na` starts at bytes 2 and 4, so `Index` finds 2 and `LastIndex` finds 4. The letter `a` appears 3 times.

slides.text:
`Split` turns one string into a slice of pieces, and `Join` does the reverse.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
Splitting is exact: two separators in a row leave an empty string between them. When the gaps vary, like repeated spaces, use `Fields`, which ignores them.

exercises.title: Split and join
exercises.guide: Cut a string into a slice at a separator, then glue the slice back together.

chunks.guide: `Split` cuts the string at every separator and returns a slice.

notes.text: One string in the slice for each piece.

chunks.guide: The separator itself is not kept in the pieces.
`Join` does the reverse. The separator goes between the items.

notes.text: Takes the slice first and the glue second.

chunks.guide: Change an item of the slice, then join it again.

output.text:
[ana eva leo] 3
ana & eva & leo
ana-bea-leo

exercises.title: Split on any spaces
exercises.guide: Split a text into words, even when the spaces are uneven.

chunks.guide: A text with extra spaces at the start, the end and between words.
Splitting on one space leaves an empty string for each extra space.
`Fields` splits around any run of white space and drops the empty pieces.

notes.text: Ignores repeated spaces, and the edges too.

chunks.guide: Tabs and newlines count as white space as well.

exercises.title: Words and dashes
exercises.guide: Turn the sentence into its words, then glue the words with dashes.

exercises.title: Split at the edges
exercises.guide: See what Split returns in unusual cases, and how to stop after a few pieces.

chunks.guide: Splitting an empty string gives one empty string, not an empty slice.
An empty separator cuts between every character.
`SplitN` makes at most n pieces. The last one keeps the rest of the string.

notes.text: The third argument is the maximum number of pieces.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the output.
exercises.explanation: Two separators in a row leave an empty string between them, so there are 3 pieces and the middle one is empty.

exercises.title: Cut at the first separator
exercises.guide: Split a setting into its key and value, and check that the separator was there.

chunks.guide: `Cut` splits at the first separator and says if it found one.

notes.text: Gives the text before, the text after and a bool.

chunks.guide: The separator is in neither half.
Without the separator, found is false.
`CutPrefix` removes a prefix and says if it was there. `CutSuffix` does the same at the end.

notes.text: Returns the rest of the string and a bool.

slides.text:
A Go string never changes. Every function here returns a new string, so keep the result in a variable. Calling one and ignoring the result does nothing.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
name = "ana"
big = upper(name)  -> "ANA"
name is still "ana"

slides.text: `Trim` removes characters from a set, while `TrimPrefix` and `TrimSuffix` remove an exact piece of text. `Map` and `FieldsFunc` take a function that decides about each rune.

exercises.title: Trim white space and characters
exercises.guide: Remove the extra characters from the ends of a string.

chunks.guide: `TrimSpace` removes white space from both ends: spaces, tabs and newlines.

notes.text: Returns a new string without the outer white space.

chunks.guide: The original string is longer than the clean one.
`Trim` removes any of the given characters from both ends.

notes.text: The second argument is a set of characters.

chunks.guide: `TrimLeft` and `TrimRight` work on one end only.

exercises.title: Remove a known prefix or suffix
exercises.guide: Remove an exact piece from the start or the end of a string.

chunks.guide: `TrimPrefix` removes the exact text from the start, once.

notes.text: Removes that exact text if the string starts with it.

chunks.guide: `TrimSuffix` does the same at the end.
If the string does not end with it, nothing changes.
`Trim` takes a set of characters, not a word. `TrimPrefix` takes the exact text.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the output.
exercises.explanation: `Trim` removes every `a` and `b` from both ends, leaving `c`. `TrimPrefix` removes the exact text `ab` once, leaving `cba`.

exercises.title: Replace text
exercises.guide: Swap a piece of a string for another.

chunks.guide: `ReplaceAll` swaps every match for the new text.

notes.text: Arguments: the text, the old piece and the new one.

chunks.text:
text := "one fish, two fish"
    changed := strings.ReplaceAll(text, "fish", "cat")
    fmt.Println(changed)

chunks.guide: `Replace` also takes how many matches to change.

notes.text: Only the first match is replaced. Use -1 for all.

chunks.guide: A string never changes: the original is still there.

output.text:
one cat, two cat
one cat, two fish
one fish, two fish

exercises.title: Case and repetition
exercises.guide: Change the case of a text and repeat a piece.

chunks.guide: `ToUpper` returns the text in capitals.

notes.text: Returns a new string in upper case.

chunks.guide: `ToLower` does the opposite.
`Repeat` joins a piece to itself the given number of times.

notes.text: Makes a longer string from copies of the first.

chunks.guide: Case changes work on any letter, not only English ones.

exercises.title: Make a slug
exercises.guide: Remove the outer white space, swap the dash for an underscore, then print it in lower case.

exercises.title: A function as the rule
exercises.guide: Pass a function that decides what to do with each character.

chunks.guide: The function gets a rune and returns the rune to use. Returning -1 drops it.

notes.text: A negative result removes the character.

chunks.guide: `Map` applies the function to every rune of the string.

notes.text: Builds a new string, one rune at a time.

chunks.guide: `FieldsFunc` splits at every rune the function says true for.

notes.text: Like Split, but the separator is any rune you choose.
